newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BZW HEAD NETS 2.8 MILLION STG IN FOUR MONTHS

Bill Harrison, head of BZW, was paid 2.8 million pounds stg by Barclays Bank, for four months work last year. Harrison, who was lured from Robert Fleming to restructure and boost performance, picked up 1.5 million stg in bonuses and 1.5 million stg in signing on fee, as well as a salary and deferred shares. He was the highest paid Barclays executive last year.
-- CHARTER FALLS TO 96 MILLION POUNDS

Welding and rail track group Charter said it still plans to make an acquisition of up to 500 million stg despite a 1.5 percent fall in underlying pre-tax profits to 96 million stg for 1996. The fall was caused by the sale of its 65 percent stake in Cape building materials business last June, making a 50 million loss.
THE TIMES
-- SINK IN KITCHEN SALES TAKES SHINE OFF LIMELIGHT SHARES

Kitchen company Limelight saw its shares fall by 25 percent following the announcement of dramatic fall in kitchen sales. The share price ended the day down 35p at 107.5p against its flotation price of 175p last November. Limelight said group sales in the first quarter of this year were down 11 percent on the previous year.
-- BG FACES WRITEDOWN OF 5 BILLION STG ON ASSETS

Owners of the British Gas GAS.L pipeline network, BG, could be facing a 5 billion stg writedown of its assets. It is expected the Monopolies and Mergers Commission will take up the Ofgas valuation of the Transco pipeline network of about 12.5 billion stg, compared to the 18 billion stg recorded in BG's current cost accounts. The move could affect the pipeline companies profits as accounting rules may not permit BG to cut its depreciation charge in line with the asset reduction.
-- INVESTORS URGED TO SACK POOR BOARD PERFORMERS

The Institute of Directors is advising shareholders that poorly performing company directors should be fired. The IoD publishes a report today on directors' remuneration, claiming it is for shareholders, especially institutional shareholders, to put pressure on the remuneration committees of companies when they disagree with their recommendations. Shareholders also should oppose the re-election of directors who do not merit their remuneration.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CASINO KEEPS BETTING OPEN

Capital Corporation, the casino operator, said a 190 million stg takeover bid from London Clubs International was dead in the water, although it admitted its fight to stay independent was not over. An improved offer from LCI, which runs seven London casinos, is expected, as well as a bid from Ladbroke, the hotel to book-makers group.
-- SAINSBURY ROASTS THE FOOD INDUSTRY

New chief executive of the Sainsbury supermarket group, Dino Adriano, attacked the food manufacturing industry for losing the confidence of consumers, and called for greater openness over food safety issues. Speaking to the annual conference of the British Retail Consortium he said the industrialisation of the food industry was responsible for the food safety crises in recent years.
-- CLARKE HOLDS DEFICIT TRUMP CARD

City analysts are predicting chancellor Kenneth Clarke will win crucial political points just before polling day by announcing a large undershoot on his budget deficit targets. New figures show the government was 3.6 billion stg in the red in February, bringing the total public sector borrowing requirement since April to 14.1 billion stg, compared with 22.2 billion stg at the same time last year. Clarke said the figures were proof that the UK was on target for a balanced budget by 2000.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- STEEL GIANT THYSSEN FIGHTS TAKEOVER BID

Krupp-Hoesch, the German steelmaker, launched a hostile 2.6 billion stg bid for its larger rival Thyssen. The move would create Europe's biggest steelmaker with combined sales of 24 billion stg and crude steel production of 18.1 million tonnes. German steel unions are concerned the takeover will prove the prelude to heavy job cuts with at least 10,000 jobs under threat.
-- SECOND WARNING SENDS DK SHARES CRASHING

Dorling Kindersley, the illustrated book and CD-Rom publisher, saw its share price fall to a three year low after publishing a warning that the strong pound, trading problems in America and an accounting change would hit profits in the year to June. The stock has been more than halved in value over the past year after Tuesday's fall of 51p to 270p.
-- REC'S HAND BIG PRICE CUTS TO 5 MILLION CUSTOMERS

Two large regional electricity companies have announced substantial price cuts from April. Eastern, part of the Energy Group, is cutting charges by between 6 percent and 9 percent and Southern is to cut around 7.2 percent off its charges. The price cuts will affect more than 5 million domestic customers.
